title: LLM judge against the agent's own ratings (not human calibration)
why: Checking a judge against a second, independent model is a cheap sanity check before (and never instead of) calibrating it against human labels.
notes: Claude Haiku judge (the live judge run) against agent rater (the coding assistant, ratings written by reading each card; not a human) on 30 rationales both graded.
Both are language models; this is not agreement with a human.
limits: Two models can share biases, so agreement does not show either is right.
Only the items both judges graded are compared; the sample is small.

The rater is the same AI coding assistant that built this project and is in the same model family as the forecasters, so its ratings carry the same blind spots; it was not blind to the judge, because it had seen some of the judge's scores earlier in the session.
These ratings do not replace the 30 human labels, which stay open.
